story: California Representative Jimmy Gomez said he will resign from Congress on 1 December after the House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence of sexual misconduct with a staffer.
title: Jimmy Gomez to resign after ethics panel misconduct findings
dek: The House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence of sexual misconduct, and the California Democrat will leave Congress on 1 December.
body:
Representative Jimmy Gomez of California said he will resign from Congress on 1 December, the same day the House Ethics Committee made public a report finding substantial evidence that he engaged in sexual misconduct with a House staffer. The bipartisan panel had adopted the report on 19 November and concluded that he made unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact toward a woman in her mid-twenties who worked in a House leadership office, not for him.

The committee said his conduct caused her serious ongoing distress and contributed to her leaving House employment in 2025. It also said the behavior could constitute misdemeanor sexual abuse under District of Columbia law, though that is an ethics finding, not a criminal charge, and none has been filed. She did not work under his supervision, but the panel said he failed to respect the power imbalance between members and staff.

She described two encounters in 2024. At a Washington bar on 29 February, she said he put his hand under her skirt and penetrated her without consent, after which she went to a bathroom and cried; later, in his office, she said he grabbed her and tried to kiss her until she refused and left. Gomez says the contact was consensual. He first mentioned only kissing, then admitted sexual contact while insisting she agreed, but the committee, which spoke with 10 witnesses, found her more credible and said he knew or had reason to know the advances were unwelcome; a second woman he named said their past relationship was consensual.

Gomez, 51, says he strongly disagrees with the report and the process, arguing that important parts of his testimony were omitted or used unfairly and that he had no chance to answer the finished document. He also said he takes responsibility for personal mistakes outside his marriage and is leaving on 1 December so staff can finish constituent casework. Democratic leaders, including Hakeem Jeffries, called the findings deeply troubling and the resignation appropriate, while lawyers for the staffer said the report confirms harassment and assault.

## A short exit after a long loss

Gomez was already on his way out. This month, fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres defeated him by about 25 points in California’s 34th District, which includes part of Los Angeles, in a race where the investigation was already public. His term would have ended on 3 January, and the ethics panel said there was not enough time left for a fuller House punishment, so the early resignation is a consequence, but a short one.

In Washington, the voters had already delivered the longer sentence. The same Monday, the committee also faulted outgoing Republicans Troy Nehls and Mike Collins for lesser problems with campaign money and office oversight. Gomez leaves on 1 December, his successor takes office with the new House in January, and the report remains, though whether it changes how members treat staff is still unanswered.
